name: old cracked asphalt road of cool charcoal grey with fine scattered non-directional aggregate specks, faded slightly warmer patches, thin crack lines, soft stains and worn broken fragments of yellow and white lane paint, its unconnected edges broken off into dirt as a chipped asphalt lip with loose asphalt chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road pieces (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, straight patch, large slab) on dirt ground

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain autotile sheet seen straight down: asphalt patches lie on a brown dirt ground, filling the full 256x192 tile. The width profile is 256 for every row. The column scans show only ground and surface texture, such as dark crack and chip lines of 1-4 rows at the patch edges. No standing volume, no front face of 3+ rows and no top surface with a front-edge line or ellipse are drawn. Each asphalt patch has only a thin dark chipped lip along its south edge, about 1-2 rows. This is correct for a terrain tile and not a standing object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's asphalt has only about 3 charcoal steps (a dark edge, a mid grey and a few specks), against 5-6 in the Beodeul paving. The dirt ground carries mottled brown patches and is reasonably textured. The asphalt patches are small, and the lane paint and cracks appear only on the right-hand sample block, as a few tiny yellow and white dashes with thin cracks. The road network pieces themselves look nearly flat dark grey with sparse specks. The edges are tinted rather than neutral, with 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is not a sticker line. The chipped lip is only a rough irregular silhouette with little loose-chunk detail. Visible tones per tile (5) are above the grass reference (3) but below the paving reference (7). Overall the asphalt is shallower than the references, with few ramp steps, little tile-by-tile highlighting and sparse variation (no warm patches, no stains). A careful artist would see it as thinner than the reference.

surfaces.part: asphalt road network pieces on dirt ground (flat terrain tiles, top-down)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tileset sheet, 256x192, fully opaque, with a brown dirt ground and grey asphalt road pieces (cross, T-junctions, dead ends, a block, a small patch, and a large crack-detail piece). It is drawn flat and top-down. The asphalt pieces have only a thin dark chipped edge line along their south sides, which is a 1-2 row lip rather than a front face of 3 or more rows. No standing volume, top band, or front face is drawn. It is terrain, so the kind matches.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 15 distinct colours across the whole board, against 80 for the grass reference. Visible tones per tile are 5, between the grass (3) and the paving (7). Near-flat coverage is 5% against 0% for both references, so there are small flat areas. The asphalt ramp is shallow, with about 3 steps: a dark charcoal body, a slightly lighter speck tone and a darker edge. The dirt ground has about 4 browns. The references carry 5-6 steps per material. The asphalt bodies are mostly even dark grey with sparse specks, and they lack per-chunk shading and clearly visible warmer faded patches. Cracks and lane paint are rare, tiny marks, mostly on a single piece. The chipped edges and loose chunks are only a rough silhouette and are not shaded one by one. Edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and reads as a dark material tone, which is fine. Overall the piece is cleaner but flatter and less dense than the Beodeul references, so it fails.

surfaces.part: asphalt road patches on dirt ground, drawn flat from above with a thin dark chipped lip along the south edges

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tile sheet: a 256x192 dirt ground with several road-network pieces (crossroads, T-junction, dead ends, a large flat patch) seen from above. The column scans show only uniform ground colour with thin 1-4 row dark edge or crack lines, and no front face of 3 or more rows. The south edge of each road piece has only a 1-row dark chipped lip. It is not a standing object, so the top-down reading fits a ground autotile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt is a flat charcoal grey with only about 3 lightness steps (base, darker edge, a few specks). It has only 5 visible tones per tile and 15 distinct colours in total, below the paving reference (7 visible tones) and the richer grass. The asphalt pieces are small, isolated blobs on a large brown dirt field, and the road network is sparse. Crack lines, yellow and white paint fragments and stains are tiny and barely visible, and the asphalt interiors read as large flat areas with little aggregate variation or warm patches. The edges are dark, chipped silhouettes, closer to a near-black sticker outline than to a tinted material tone, though the measured neutral share is 0%. Overall the piece is shallower than the Beodeul references in shading ramp and surface texture.

surfaces.part: asphalt road patches on dirt ground (flat terrain tileset)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tileset sheet, not a standing object. It is 256 px wide and 192 rows tall, and shows flat asphalt road pieces (crossroad, T-junctions, dead ends, a large fill block) on brown dirt. The asphalt reads as a flat ground surface viewed from above. Each piece has only a thin dark chipped lip of 1-2 rows along its south edge, with no front face of 3 or more rows. The column scan shows uniform dirt and asphalt bands with no top/front structure. For terrain this is a flat top-down read, which is expected for ground tiles.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 15 colours in total and 5 visible tones per tile. That sits between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7), and 5% near-flat coverage is low. By eye, though, the asphalt reads as a mostly uniform dark charcoal with sparse specks. It has about 3 lightness steps, with no per-chunk highlights and little of the warmer faded patching or soft staining the brief describes. The cracks are a few thin dark strokes and the yellow/white paint is only a couple of tiny flecks, so they add little information. The dirt has some mottling in about 3-4 browns, which is better but still coarse next to Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material. Edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and counts as dark material tone. The chipped lip shapes are reasonable, but the road patches look like flat sticker-like cutouts with little internal shading. Overall the piece is shallower than the references, and when in doubt this fails.
